parts.name: Mouth_Neck_Blue
parts.method: REVISED 2026-07-30 (Mouth physical-chain restoration task), supersedes the 2026-07-29 t=(0,-20.9,0) 'zero-length transitional element' simplification (kept in 'finding' for history). This session measured Mouth_Neck_Blue's own geometry directly rather than treating it as zero-length: (a) sharp-edge ring extraction (>20deg) found no clean axisymmetric ball-cup or peg feature -- the tilted ring initially suspected of being a ball-socket cup (n=158, r=7.637mm near local y=4.8) was checked against a convex-hull-vs-own-volume concavity test (ratio 0.949, max recess depth 4.5mm) and the recess turned out to be centered at y=[-8.0,-3.5] under the WIDE flange, not near y=4.8 -- i.e. that tilted ring is just a curvature-discontinuity on an otherwise convex taper, not a socket rim. (b) trimesh.section() radius-profile scan confirms the part is a plain two-ended connector: a wide flange (y=-8.046 local, r=12.35mm, close to Ball's own 25.1mm diameter) at one end, a narrow tapering tip (y=+8.046 local, shrinking to r~2.2mm) at the other, joined by a waist/bulge with a shallow (~4.4mm) blind bore under the flange (not a through-passage -- matches hardware/src/make_audio.py's own comment that Neck/Ball are natively solid/near-solid). (c) Orientation was fixed by elimination: attaching the wide flange to Cannon's rear face makes Neck's own body geometrically overlap Cannon's own solid barrel (found by trying this direction first); attaching the narrow tip to Cannon's rear face (diameter class matches the tip's own taper, and the rear hole itself measures r=5.351mm -- see Mouth_Cannon_Grey entry) does not overlap. Neck is therefore placed with its tip end flush against Cannon's rear face (t.y = CANNON_Y_REAR-NECK_TIP_Y_150 = -20.926-8.046 = -28.972) and its wide flange end (at local y=-8.046, i.e. Cannon-local y=-37.018) touching Mouth_Ball_Grey's own surface -- using Neck's own unambiguous full axial length NECK_AXIAL_LEN_150=16.092mm (Y bbox extent) as the Ball-to-Cannon standoff, consistent with this kit's other non-precision butt-glued joints (Claw_Grey, TailJoint sleeve).
parts.confidence: medium (Neck's own axial length and end-diameters: direct STL measurement; the flush-contact/0mm-insertion treatment of both ends and the choice of which end faces which part are reasoned simplifications, cross-checked by elimination of the geometrically-impossible reverse orientation but not independently forensically pinned down further -- see Mouth_Cannon_Grey entry's method note on the residual <0.9mm insertion-depth question)

parts.method:
2026-07-28 v3 re-fit (review finding major#7, supersedes the v2 matrix above -- v2 kept in history below): scipy.optimize.differential_evolution, same 6 params/bounds/z-band as v2, cost = mean((signed_distance-1.0mm)^2) + 3.0*mean(clip(-signed_distance,0,None)^2) -- i.e. v2's cost plus a protrusion penalty so outlier float vertices are no longer 'free' to the optimizer. Verified on the FULL 1107-vertex guard mesh: 917/1107 (82.8%) inside the shell (sd>=0), max embed 7.44mm, max float 6.55mm (v2 was 73.0%/7.33mm/6.90mm), median sd=1.58mm, p05=-1.18mm/p95=4.62mm (v2: median 1.08mm, p05=-1.51mm, p95=4.24mm). Kept as the new placement since it is better or equal on every metric except p95 (+0.38mm, minor) and max embed (+0.11mm, negligible).

This entry was regenerated from scratch against the restored geometry using a principled, single-parameter construction instead: (1) ORIENTATION: align the toe's known local -Y axis (root->tip, established via a y-axis cross-section scan: cross-section shrinks from ~13.5x5.5mm at y=+8.375 (root, bbox max) to a point at y=-8.375 (tip, bbox min) -- unchanged from the prior session's finding) to the stub's own outward axis F = normalize(tip - base), where base/tip are measured directly on the ACTUAL BUILT hardware/stl/leg_foot_bored.stl via trimesh.slice_plane at the stub's widest pre-merge cross-section (z=-6.87 local, just below where the 3 stub fragments coalesce into the main pad at z=-6.86) and the fragment's own apex vertex (min-z point), both to native STL vertex precision. This leaves exactly one rotational DOF (roll about F) undetermined; it is fixed by a second, independently-justified criterion -- see (2). (2) ROLL: the toe's local -Z axis is the 'belly' (concave, ground-facing) side -- confirmed by a fresh y-axis cross-section sweep this session: the mesh's own lowest point is not at the tip (y=-8.375) but partway along the shaft (y=-4.657, z=-3.658), i.e. the claw's underside bulges downward before the tip curls back up, a classic talon/hook profile (matches the visible black claws in the kit's completed-build photo, Auxiliaries/.thumbnails/thumbnail_middle.png inside TACHIKOMA.3mf: claws droop from the grey ankle cuff and their tips curl toward the ground). Roll is chosen so this local -Z axis maps as close to world -Z (straight down) as the F-alignment constraint allows: D = normalize((0,0,-1) - dot((0,0,-1),F)*F) (down projected perpendicular to F), and the full right-handed orthonormal frame is R = columns[F x D, -F, -D] (verified: R@(0,-1,0)==F, R@(0,0,-1)==D, det(R)==+1, i.e. a proper rotation, not a reflection). A clean corollary confirmed numerically: the resulting local-X (E_x = F x D) always comes out exactly horizontal (z-component identically 0, since D is by construction a linear combination of F and the world Z axis) -- i.e. this convention keeps the claw's left-right axis level, the natural choice for a belly-down claw. (3) TRANSLATION (1 remaining parameter, 'standoff'): first confirmed via a y-axis cross-section scan of Leg_Toe_Black_x12.stl (n_interiors=0 at every slice from the root face y=8.375 down to y=6.0) that there is NO deep socket/bore at the root -- it is a flat-ish solid face that glues over/around the small locating peg (this matches and independently reproduces the prior session's same conclusion). Given no snap-fit feature exists, the toe's true root edge (raw bbox y=+8.375, Y0 below) is registered AT the stub's measured base point with ZERO artificial push (standoff=0mm, i.e. translation = stub_base + Y0*F exactly -- this is the tightest defensible placement, not a tuned/searched value): a standoff sweep from -1.0 to +2.0mm (0.1mm steps, boolean intersection against the actual leg_foot_bored.stl) shows standoff=0 already gives <5% toe-foot overlap for all 3 stubs (4.93/4.77/4.79%) and exactly 0.0 toe-toe overlap -- so no push was needed to clear the existing <5% glue-allowance threshold this file already uses for this same purpose (see finding). The residual ~4.8-4.9% overlap at standoff=0 is not a placement error -- it is the geometric consequence of a flat root edge sitting against the paw's locally-curved (domed) surface, present at any standoff and only slowly shrinking as standoff grows (was still ~2.8-3% even at standoff=+2.0mm) because the mating faces are not shaped to match (kit design: no complementary socket). Toe id mapping (unchanged from before): _0=FRONT stub (tip_ang approx -98.4 deg local), _1=LEFT stub (approx +145.4 deg), _2=RIGHT stub (approx +45.5 deg) -- same per-slot matrix reused across all 4 legs (FR/FL/RL/RR), matching this file's convention elsewhere.
